docs.title: OpenMed Agent documentation
docs.text:
Terminal-native AI for clinical workflows. Install the agent, choose a lane, and keep every plan, tool call, and artifact inspectable.

OpenMed Agent 1.0 is the final release. Hosted services stay available on an as-available basis and may change, be interrupted, or be discontinued; see Long-Term Use.

$ openmed config provider-set openai --api-key "sk-..."
$ openmed

docs.title: The system at a glance
docs.text:
OpenMed separates the operator runtime, the model-provider path, and the medical service tier — visible, configurable, and suited to sensitive or high-volume clinical processing.

PLANE 01 · LOCALOperator runtime

Sessions, plans, tool traces, provenance, and workflow artifacts stay on the machine running OpenMed.

operator-controlledvisible-review PLANE 02 · PROTECTEDClinical extraction & de-identification

NER, PII detection, and de-identification run through a dedicated native service endpoint.

protected-extractionPII-aware PLANE 03 · PROTECTEDTerminology, coding & HCC

Semantic search, validation, crosswalks, drug safety, risk adjustment, and comorbidity scoring across ICD-10, CPT, SNOMED CT, LOINC, HCC, and other reference sets.

See Native Medical Services for the deployment story, and the product page for dataset coverage numbers.

docs.title: Audit Trail
docs.text:
OpenMed can write an opt-in audit trail for agent runs. It is off by default.

The audit trail is for operators who need durable evidence of what happened across runs: which model path was used, which tools ran, whether they succeeded, how long they took, and which prompts/results were captured or fingerprinted. It is not telemetry. OpenMed does not send audit data to OpenMed infrastructure.

docs.title: Storage options
docs.text:
OpenMed supports three audit destinations:

Destination Use when Notes hf_dataset You want versioned private audit history on Hugging Face Hub Recommended default. Each raw run is committed as JSON under runs/YYYY/MM/DD/, with one root Agent Trace Viewer-compatible *.jsonl file per session. hf_bucket You want private mutable object storage on Hugging Face If a bucket write fails, OpenMed falls back to local traces. local You want offline-only audit traces Writes under ~/.openmed/traces by default.

HF datasets are useful for audit because they can be private, access-controlled, versioned, and easy to inspect in the Hub UI. HF buckets are useful when you prefer object-storage semantics over dataset history.

Destinations must be private

OpenMed creates a new dataset or bucket as private, and it refuses to upload to one that is not private. It never changes a destination's visibility. A refused trace is kept in local storage when the local fallback is on.

docs.title: Enable audit
docs.text:
For a private Hugging Face dataset:

export OPENMED_AUDIT_HF_TOKEN=hf_...
openmed audit enable --destination hf_dataset --dataset "<user-or-org>/openmed-traces"
openmed audit status

For a local-only trace store:

openmed audit enable --destination local

For a private Hugging Face bucket:

export OPENMED_AUDIT_HF_TOKEN=hf_...
openmed audit enable --destination hf_bucket --bucket "<bucket-name>"

openmed audit enable writes a test trace to the destination first. Pass --no-smoke-test to skip it.

If the HF write fails during an agent run, the trace is saved locally instead. Audit failures never stop the agent run. Local traces are plain JSON files that use your default file permissions, so protect that folder.

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
OpenMed stores audit config in ~/.openmed/audit.json:

{
  "enabled": true,
  "schema_version": "1.0",
  "destination": "hf_dataset",
  "phi_payload": "payload",
  "flush_mode": "per_run",
  "hf": {
    "repo": "my-org/openmed-traces",
    "token_env": "OPENMED_AUDIT_HF_TOKEN"
  },
  "local": {
    "path": "~/.openmed/traces",
    "fallback_on_hf_failure": true
  }
}

A bucket destination uses "destination": "hf_bucket" and "bucket" in the hf section instead of "repo".

Use token_env instead of a literal token whenever possible. A token you pass with --token or type at the prompt is stored in this file as token_literal. With no configured token, OpenMed uses HF_TOKEN or your local Hugging Face login.

docs.title: PHI payload modes
docs.text:
Audit capture is independent of PHI mode. PHI mode describes the operator posture for the run. phi_payload controls what the audit trace stores.

Mode What the trace stores none Metadata only. No input/output fingerprints. fingerprint Metadata plus SHA-256 fingerprints. preview Fingerprints plus short best-effort redacted previews. Long values are intentionally clipped. payload Full raw input/output payloads. This is the default once audit is enabled.

The default payload mode is intended for complete private audit trails, so any PHI in your prompts and tool output goes to the audit destination. Use preview for short snippets, fingerprint when you only need to show that the same payload was used later, or none for metadata-only traces.

These modes have limits:

  • preview uses simple pattern replacement, not the PII service. Names and other identifiers can remain in a snippet.
  • fingerprint hashes are unsalted, so a short or guessable value can be confirmed by hashing candidates.
  • Error messages from failed tools are stored in every mode, up to 1,000 characters.
  • extract_pii and deidentify_text calls are reduced to counts and status in every mode. Other tools, including deidentify_batch, follow phi_payload.
openmed audit set-phi-payload preview
# Restore full private transcripts and tool payloads:
openmed audit set-phi-payload payload

docs.title: Runtime commands
docs.text:
openmed audit status
openmed audit verify
openmed audit show --last 10
openmed audit show <run_id>
openmed audit export <run_id> --out trace.json
openmed audit local-list
openmed audit local-sync
openmed audit open
openmed audit set-flush-mode per_run
openmed audit pause
openmed audit resume
openmed audit disable

local-sync pushes local traces to a configured hf_dataset destination only. open prints the destination URL.

Inside the TUI, /audit shows the active status, destination, PHI payload mode, fallback path, and relevant CLI commands. The status line shows audit: off, audit: syncing ..., audit: ✓ ..., audit: ⚠ local-only, audit: ⚠ paused, or audit: ⚠ error. TUI audit uploads run in the background so slow Hugging Face writes do not block the interactive run-completion path.

docs.title: Trace contents
docs.text:
Each run trace includes:

  • OpenMed version, run ID, timestamps, duration, and host fingerprint
  • Agent mode, access mode, PHI mode, model provider, model name, and reasoning effort
  • Prompt fingerprint, and optionally preview or payload depending on phi_payload
  • Session transcript messages captured during the run, including user messages, assistant messages, plans/cards, and tool messages when available
  • Tool-call actions with input/output fingerprints, status, latency, and error fingerprints
  • Full tool output payloads in payload mode, including large outputs expanded from persisted local tool-result files when available
  • Provider usage actions when the SDK reports token accounting
  • Summary counts for actions, tools, model calls, and errors

OpenMed writes schema.json to new HF dataset destinations so teams can validate trace shape outside the app. HF dataset repos also get root *.jsonl trace files tagged as agent-traces, matching the layout used by public Agent Trace Viewer datasets. Those root JSONL files are stable per session and are updated as the session grows, so the Dataset Viewer row represents one session. The exact immutable OpenMed audit JSON for each run remains in runs/.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Variable Purpose OPENMED_AUDIT_ENABLED Runtime override for audit on/off OPENMED_AUDIT_DESTINATION hf_dataset, hf_bucket, local, or none OPENMED_AUDIT_HF_TOKEN HF token used for private dataset or bucket writes OPENMED_AUDIT_HF_REPO Private HF dataset repo OPENMED_AUDIT_HF_BUCKET Private HF bucket name OPENMED_AUDIT_PHI_PAYLOAD none, fingerprint, preview, or payload OPENMED_AUDIT_FLUSH_MODE per_run writes to the destination after each run. manual writes traces locally until you run openmed audit local-sync OPENMED_AUDIT_LOCAL_FALLBACK 1 or 0 OPENMED_AUDIT_LOCAL_PATH Local fallback trace path OPENMED_AUDIT_CONFIG_PATH Read the audit configuration from a different path

docs.title: Batch Inference
docs.text:
OpenMed can submit a large set of independent inference requests to a remote batch provider, return immediately, and resume the job from another process. Doubleword is the supported batch provider.

For interactive streaming or individual async requests, see Doubleword real-time and Responses. All modes share the same key.

Batch inference is separate from the interactive Agent TUI. It does not run OpenMed tools or a multi-turn agent loop. Each JSONL row is one direct chat-completions or embeddings request.

There is no Doubleword batch screen or /batch command in the TUI. Run openmed batch in a second terminal while using the TUI. The TUI's /privacy-batch command is a separate clinical privacy workflow.

docs.title: Why use a 24-hour batch?
docs.text:
Use batching when you have many independent records and can trade response time for a lower inference price. Your submission returns a job ID immediately; the provider schedules the work and you collect the results later. 24h is the completion window for each submitted batch, not a mandatory 24-hour sleep or a promise that a multi-stage workflow will finish overnight.

Workload One request per What you collect later Retrospective coding-quality review Closed encounter plus prepared NLP/ICD-10/HCC evidence Draft discrepancies and a human-review queue Scheduled research-corpus screening Abstract or document chunk Inclusion labels, evidence quotes, and reasons for review Backlog document enrichment Previously collected document Structured metadata or a draft summary Offline regression evaluation Fixed synthetic test case Model outputs to grade and compare with earlier runs

These workloads tolerate delayed results. A live consultation, urgent triage, an interactive TUI turn, or an action waiting on the next model response usually needs a synchronous provider instead.

Check Doubleword's model pages for batch and real-time prices, availability, and how cached tokens are counted. Batching covers model inference only; native NLP and coding service calls run separately.

docs.title: A useful overnight workflow
docs.text:
For a chart backlog, prepare each encounter's permitted source text and run the NLP, code-validation, and HCC reference lookups first. Keep their real outputs, failures, model year, and provenance. Package that evidence into one independent model request per encounter asking for a source-grounded audit draft. Submit the file, close your terminal, and collect the review queue the next day. Separate unsupported diagnoses and missing service evidence for human review; do not automatically turn model drafts into claims or clinical decisions. Pin the coding model, payment year, and service reference-data version for the workload. Check representative HCC mappings against the corresponding official reference release: a successful tool response or echoed model name does not verify the underlying mapping data or RAF calculation. Keep that validation separate from checks that the model followed its instructions.

The medical lookups need working native medical services. Doubleword credentials alone do not provide them. openmed agent --once can run the lookups from a script; see CLI workflows. Label HCC and RAF results as mechanical references for unreviewed codes, so the model audits the import rather than mistaking a mapping for clinical support, and keep service failures visible in the evidence.

Once the JSONL file is ready, a single batch window is all it takes:

openmed batch validate overnight-audit.jsonl
openmed batch submit overnight-audit.jsonl --description "closed-encounter review"
# Save the returned job ID. Later, or from a scheduled job:
openmed batch status <job-id>
openmed batch results <job-id> --json

Build each row with a Doubleword generation model in body.model, such as deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, stable custom_id values, and a suitable output-token limit. Join results to source records by custom_id, never by output order. Inspect row errors as well as the overall job status, and retry only explicitly failed records after reconciliation. The CLI sends the JSONL you prepare; it does not automatically gather medical evidence or execute tools.

A model-driven tool loop needs a local orchestrator to execute returned tool calls and then submit another batch with the receipts. Every dependent batch has its own completion window: nine serial stages could span nine such windows. For economical overnight processing, prepare deterministic service evidence before the batch and minimize dependent model stages.

When interpreting service evidence, distinguish request success from supported coding. NLP entity spans may include negated or family-history mentions. A code validator's valid field may describe syntax while exists and billable are false. A successful HCC lookup only says how a code maps; it does not establish that the encounter supports that code. Keep these fields and the original note in the review evidence instead of converting every successful service call into an accepted diagnosis.

docs.title: Configure Doubleword
docs.text:
Set the key in the environment:

export DOUBLEWORD_API_KEY="sk-..."

Or store it in OpenMed's private provider-secret file:

openmed config provider-set doubleword --api-key "sk-..."
openmed config provider-show

Alternatively, this ~/.openmed/provider_secrets.json entry references the exported environment variable (replace the reference with a literal key to store it in the file):

{
  "provider": {
    "doubleword": {
      "options": {
        "apiKey": "{env:DOUBLEWORD_API_KEY}"
      }
    }
  }
}

The environment variable takes precedence over the stored value. The Doubleword endpoint is fixed to https://api.doubleword.ai/v1; there is no base-URL setting for this hosted provider. OpenMed sends this key only to that host and never writes it into batch state, result files, or CLI output. Batch commands use this file for credentials. Its optional interactive models list does not rewrite the models in your JSONL. openmed batch submit selects batch processing; an individual flex request uses openmed responses submit instead. There is no async flag to set in provider secrets. Merge the doubleword entry inside an existing provider object when other providers are configured.

docs.title: Create a JSONL input file
docs.text:
Save the following two lines as requests.jsonl. Each line is an independent OpenAI-style request. custom_id must be unique in the file and is how you join a result back to its source record.

{"custom_id":"case-001","method":"POST","url":"/v1/chat/completions","body":{"model":"deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Return only the word OK."}],"max_tokens":4096}}
{"custom_id":"case-002","method":"POST","url":"/v1/chat/completions","body":{"model":"deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash","messages":[{"role":"user","content":"Return only the word READY."}],"max_tokens":4096}}

Use a model ID available to your Doubleword account. OpenMed does not replace, route, or silently correct model IDs inside the request body. For reasoning models, the output budget also covers reasoning tokens. A tiny budget can produce finish_reason: "length" with no final text even when the request succeeds; inspect each result's finish reason and message content.

Validate before spending credits:

openmed batch validate requests.jsonl

Validation is local and does not require a key or network connection. It checks UTF-8 JSONL structure, unique IDs, request method, endpoint consistency, body.model, file size, request count, and disallows nested streaming.

docs.title: Submit and resume
docs.text:
Submission uploads the file, creates the remote batch, saves the returned IDs, and exits. It does not wait for the provider to finish.

openmed batch submit requests.jsonl --description "nightly extraction"

The command prints an OpenMed local job ID such as batch-20260927T210000Z-12ab34cd. Use either that local ID or the Doubleword batch ID with subsequent commands:

openmed batch status  batch-20260927T210000Z-12ab34cd
openmed batch results batch-20260927T210000Z-12ab34cd
openmed batch wait    batch-20260927T210000Z-12ab34cd
openmed batch cancel  batch-20260927T210000Z-12ab34cd
openmed batch list

status refreshes provider state. results refreshes state and downloads any new output and error records. wait polls, downloads partial results as they become available, and stops at completed, failed, expired, or cancelled. Stopping wait with Ctrl+C affects only the local waiter; the remote job remains resumable. Cancellation is a best-effort provider request, and results already processed remain downloadable. status --no-refresh reads local state without a network request. list shows up to 20 local jobs; --limit changes that number, and --refresh updates jobs that are still running.

To submit and wait in one command:

openmed batch submit requests.jsonl --wait --poll-interval 10

For automation, every command that returns a job accepts --json. A bounded wait can be resumed later:

openmed batch wait <job-id> --timeout 900 --json

Wait intervals must be finite and at least one second; timeouts must be finite and positive. Omitting --timeout waits without a local deadline. A single HTTP request can outlast that deadline until its network timeout expires. Invalid wait options are rejected before submission. submit --wait prints the saved job ID to stderr before waiting, including when --json is selected.

wait and submit --wait exit 0 for a completed job with no reported failed rows, 1 for unsuccessful terminal outcomes or row failures, 2 for validation, provider, or wait-timeout errors, and 130 on Ctrl+C. Commands such as status return 0 when the inspection succeeds, even if the inspected job has failed. Always inspect both the batch status and per-row errors.

docs.title: Partial results and local files
docs.text:
Doubleword exposes output and error files while a job is still processing. OpenMed uses the provider's X-Last-Line cursor to request later chunks and also deduplicates records by custom_id, so repeating results does not append the same row twice.

One process at a time can update a job. Concurrent updates return a busy error; retry after the other command finishes its current request. Result files are replaced atomically before cursors are saved, so interrupted local writes can be retried without leaving partial JSON lines.

By default, one job lives at:

~/.openmed/batches/<local-job-id>/
├── job.json
├── input.jsonl
├── output.jsonl     # appears after the first successful result
└── errors.jsonl     # appears after the first failed result

The job directory is mode 0700; state, input, and result files are mode 0600. job.json contains provider IDs, status, counts, result cursors, timestamps, models, and the input digest. It never contains the API key or an authorization header. Override the root with OPENMED_BATCH_DIR when a job store belongs on a different encrypted or managed volume.

Keep the local job directory until you have retrieved the records you need. Remote result files have an expiry timestamp in the provider response and may not remain downloadable indefinitely.

If submission fails after the provider may have accepted it, check Doubleword's dashboard before submitting again. A local submission_failed state does not prove no remote job exists; paid creation requests are never retried automatically.

docs.title: Limits and endpoints
docs.text:
The Doubleword adapter enforces the provider's published input limits before upload:

Contract Value Maximum input file 200 MiB Maximum requests 50,000 JSONL rows Maximum custom_id length 64 characters Completion window 24h Supported row URLs /v1/chat/completions, /v1/embeddings

Select embeddings explicitly, and use the same URL in every row:

openmed batch validate embeddings.jsonl --endpoint /v1/embeddings
openmed batch submit embeddings.jsonl --endpoint /v1/embeddings

Embedding rows use a Doubleword embedding model in body.model. See Doubleword's Batch Inference documentation for its service contract and model catalog for account-visible model IDs.

docs.title: Data boundary
docs.text: Submitting a file sends every row body to Doubleword and to the infrastructure serving the selected model. The local copy is private on disk, but it is not automatically de-identified. Do not assume TUI PHI mode or the file-privacy workflow transforms batch JSONL; prepare the body content for the remote provider before submission and apply your organization's data-use, retention, region, and provider-agreement requirements.

docs.title: CLI Reference
docs.text: openmed is both the default TUI launcher and the command-line surface for authentication, configuration, asynchronous inference batches, MCP management, profiles, and updates.

docs.title: Top-level commands
docs.text: Command What it does openmed Launch the interactive TUI with the current defaults openmed agent Launch the TUI, or run one headless tool workflow with --once openmed --models List the TUI model catalog openmed --version Print the installed version openmed --license Print the OpenMed Agent license openmed config provider-set ... Store a provider API key (recommended sign-in) openmed login Start the experimental ChatGPT sign-in browser flow openmed codex ... Codex auth commands: login, status, logout openmed oauth ... The same auth commands under another name openmed config ... Inspect or persist config values openmed batch ... Validate, submit, resume, retrieve, or cancel asynchronous inference batches openmed responses ... Submit and resume Doubleword async flex or on-demand priority Responses openmed mcp ... Add, enable, disable, or diagnose remote MCP servers openmed audit ... Configure and inspect opt-in private audit traces openmed update Check for and install an update (openmed --update does the same) openmed env Print environment/debug information

docs.title: Launch the agent
docs.text:
# Default launch
openmed

# Pick a model and reasoning effort
openmed --model gpt-6.1-sol
openmed agent --model gpt-6.1-sol --reasoning-effort medium
openmed agent --model gpt-6.1-sol --reasoning-effort high

# Xiaomi MiMo token plan (key configured separately)
openmed agent --provider mimo
openmed agent --provider mimo --model mimo-v2.6-flash --reasoning-effort none

# Doubleword real-time agent (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash by default)
openmed agent --provider doubleword

# List available models
openmed --models

# Start in consumer mode
openmed agent --agent consumer --skill analyzing-health-data

# Start in care-coordination mode
openmed agent --agent coordination --skill care-coordination

# Preload a built-in or user skill
openmed agent --skill reviewing-prior-auth

# Start with all configured MCP servers enabled
openmed --mcp-enabled

docs.title: Run without the TUI
docs.text:
openmed agent --provider doubleword --once 'List the available coding workflows.'
openmed agent --provider doubleword --once - --json --timeout 600 < prompt.txt > result.json

--once runs the provider's real agent/tool loop and exits. Progress goes to stderr; stdout contains the final answer or one JSON result. See headless workflows for permissions and exit codes. Direct responses/batch commands remain inference-only and do not execute tools.

docs.title: Agent flags
docs.text:
These flags belong to openmed agent. Plain openmed accepts --model, --models, --agent, --session, and --auto-approve; use openmed agent for the rest.

Flag Behavior --model Model name passed into the active SDK. Default: the saved model, otherwise gpt-6.1-sol. With --provider, the provider's default applies: claude-sonnet-4-6 on Anthropic, mimo-v2.5-pro on MiMo, the first configured model on OpenRouter (otherwise qwen/qwen3.8-27b) and Doubleword (otherwise deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash), and the first configured endpoint on custom --models Print available TUI models and exit -s, --session ID Resume a saved TUI session. Rejected with --once --once PROMPT Run one headless request; - reads stdin --json With --once, emit the final result and tool receipts as JSON --timeout With --once, cancel after this many seconds (default 600) --permission-mode With --once, override the mode: auto, plan, or denyall --file-privacy With --once, select off, on, or auto host file restrictions --reasoning-effort Model-aware reasoning effort; default: the saved setting, otherwise medium; GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra support low through max; GPT-6 Sol/Luna also support none; MiMo uses none for thinking off and other values for thinking on. extra_high is accepted as an alias for xhigh --skill Preload a skill by ID --phi-mode PHI mode for the session: full, deid, or strict. deid and strict are enforced. --once supports full only --agent Agent mode: clinical, consumer, coordination, or default --provider Force a provider: openai, anthropic, openrouter, mimo, doubleword, or custom. Omit to select from the model and configured auth --auto-approve Skip tool approval prompts and log each one. Workflow final-write review is never bypassed. Also set by OPENMED_AUTO_APPROVE=1

--json, --timeout, --permission-mode, and --file-privacy require --once; without it the command exits with code 2.

default is the same as clinical. There are three agent modes: clinical, consumer, and coordination.

docs.title: Top-level flags
docs.text:
These go before any subcommand:

Flag Behavior --mcp-enabled Enable every MCP server in your config. The change is saved, so the servers stay enabled on later runs --config-path PATH Use another general config file for this command --update Same as openmed update --check-update Same as openmed update --check

docs.title: Individual async and on-demand requests
docs.text:
openmed responses submit request.json --service-tier flex
openmed responses submit request.json --service-tier priority --wait --timeout 120
openmed responses list
openmed responses status <response-id>
openmed responses wait <response-id> --poll-interval 5 --timeout 300
openmed responses results <response-id>
openmed responses adopt <remote-response-id>

These commands use the Doubleword Responses API, separate from JSONL batches. request.json must contain model, input, and max_output_tokens; see Doubleword for a complete example. The key comes from DOUBLEWORD_API_KEY or provider secrets; the execution tier comes from --service-tier (default flex). --wait only waits locally. Neither flag is a persistent provider-secret setting or a TUI mode switch. Results include tool calls but do not execute them. For streaming agent tool loops use openmed agent --provider doubleword. Its reasoning behavior uses model defaults; the TUI effort setting does not override Doubleword reasoning.

docs.title: Authentication
docs.text:
An OpenAI API key is the recommended way to use OpenAI models (see Providers). ChatGPT sign-in is experimental:

# API key (recommended)
openmed config provider-set openai --api-key "sk-..."

# Experimental ChatGPT sign-in
openmed login

# Status
openmed codex status
openmed oauth status

# Logout
openmed codex logout
openmed codex logout --all

openmed login accepts -f / --force to clear existing credentials first, --no-browser to print the sign-in URL, and --timeout <seconds> for the browser redirect (default 300). openmed codex logout --all also removes any stale auth files.

Storage:

  • openmed login writes ~/.openmed/auth.json
  • --global is accepted and has no effect
  • Auth detection uses ~/.openmed/auth.json
  • A project-local ./auth.json is ignored

Provider credentials — API keys, ~/.openmed/provider_secrets.json, and the OpenRouter/Doubleword model lists — are documented on the Providers page. The commands are:

openmed config provider-set openai     --api-key "sk-..."
openmed config provider-set anthropic  --api-key "sk-ant-..."
openmed config provider-set openrouter --api-key "sk-or-..." \
  --models "qwen/qwen3.8-27b,z-ai/glm-5.2"
openmed config provider-set mimo      --api-key "tp-..."
openmed config provider-set doubleword --api-key "sk-..."
openmed config provider-set custom --base-url http://localhost:8000/v1 --model <served-model-id>
openmed config provider-show
openmed config openrouter-models --search qwen   # browse the OpenRouter catalog

Each also accepts --unset-api-key; provider-set openai, anthropic, openrouter, doubleword and custom additionally accept --models and --unset-models. provider-set custom needs --base-url and --model together, and --remove-model <id> removes an endpoint; see Custom endpoints. For OpenAI and Anthropic the list adds models newer than the built-in catalog to /model (OPENAI_MODELS / ANTHROPIC_MODELS override it). Environment variables OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_API_KEY, MIMO_API_KEY, and DOUBLEWORD_API_KEY are equivalent and take precedence over the file.

Save the default model for new sessions, so that --model is not needed on every launch:

openmed config model-set gpt-6.1-sol --provider openai --reasoning-effort high
openmed config model-unset

The values are stored as model, provider and reasoning_effort in ~/.openmed/settings.json; flags still override them for one run. See Default model and newer models.

Doubleword offers 11 built-in generation models. A configured list replaces them in /model and --models, and its first entry becomes the interactive default. DOUBLEWORD_MODELS overrides the stored list. See the model IDs and provider-secret example.

MiMo needs only the key: its endpoint and all four native models are built in. provider-set mimo does not accept --base-url or --models. See complete MiMo provider secrets examples.

Provider config is loaded once per process. If you edit the file manually, restart OpenMed.

docs.title: Asynchronous batch inference
docs.text:
Batches run on Doubleword. Validation is offline; submission returns immediately with a durable local ID.

openmed batch validate requests.jsonl
openmed batch submit requests.jsonl
openmed batch status <job-id>
openmed batch results <job-id>  # downloads new partial output/error rows
openmed batch wait <job-id>
openmed batch cancel <job-id>
openmed batch list

Use --json for automation. submit --wait combines creation and polling; wait --timeout <seconds> stops the local waiter without cancelling the remote job. The complete JSONL contract, storage layout, provider-secret example, and privacy boundary are in Batch Inference.

docs.title: Model selection
docs.text:
The built-in catalog, also printed by openmed --models, includes:

Model Notes claude-fable-5-1 Claude Fable 5.1; demanding reasoning and long-running work claude-opus-5-5 Claude Opus 5.5 claude-opus-5 Claude Opus 5 claude-sonnet-5 Claude Sonnet 5 claude-opus-4-8 Claude Opus 4.8 claude-sonnet-4-6 Anthropic provider default claude-haiku-5-5 Claude Haiku 5.5 gpt-6.1-sol Default; coding and agentic workflows; medium reasoning gpt-6-astra Next-generation flagship GPT-6 model gpt-6-sol GPT-6 model for complex coding and agentic workflows gpt-6-luna Fast, cost-efficient GPT-6 model mimo-v2.5-pro MiMo token-plan default; text input mimo-v2.5 MiMo token plan; text and image input mimo-v2.6-pro MiMo token plan; text and image input mimo-v2.6-flash MiMo token plan; text input

With a MiMo key configured, the MiMo group offers all four models automatically. Bare MiMo model IDs select the token-plan route; a namespaced xiaomi/... ID selects OpenRouter.

With an OpenRouter key configured, the switcher adds an OpenRouter group listing your configured models (--models, OPENROUTER_MODELS, or the qwen/qwen3.8-27b default) with capability chips such as vision · 1M ctx · reasoning. Models that cannot call tools are marked incompatible and refused at startup.

Doubleword adds its own group of 11 models when its key is configured.

At runtime you can switch models with /model, or Ctrl+M on terminals that report it separately from Enter.

The picker flow is:

  1. Model
  2. Reasoning effort
  3. Reasoning summary on supported models

GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra offer low, medium, high, xhigh, and max. GPT-6 Sol and Luna also offer none, which skips the reasoning-summary step. On GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra, --reasoning-effort none maps to low. The app defaults to GPT-6.1 Sol with medium reasoning and thinking display off.

docs.title: Native medical services
docs.text:
Many OpenMed capabilities are native tools from the agent's perspective, even when they call configured HTTP services behind the scenes.

  • extract_entities, extract_pii, deidentify_text, and the batch extraction helpers use the native extraction service plane
  • ICD-10, CPT, SNOMED, LOINC, HCC, RAF, and terminology/crosswalk tools use the native coding and terminology service plane
  • PubMed, MedlinePlus, and RxNorm lookups go from your machine directly to those public APIs by default (OPENMED_MED_CODES_EXECUTION_MODE=server sends them through the coding service)
  • Standard builds use OpenMed-hosted native services without extra local setup; see Native Medical Services to use your own servers

These are native OpenMed tools. They are not MCP tools.

docs.title: Audit traces
docs.text:
Audit is off by default. When enabled, OpenMed writes one private trace per agent run to the configured destination.

# Private HF dataset, recommended for versioned history
export OPENMED_AUDIT_HF_TOKEN=hf_...
openmed audit enable --destination hf_dataset --dataset "<user-or-org>/openmed-traces"

# Local-only audit traces
openmed audit enable --destination local

# Inspect status and traces
openmed audit status
openmed audit show --last 10
openmed audit export <run_id> --out trace.json

Useful audit commands:

Command What it does openmed audit enable Create or configure the audit destination and write ~/.openmed/audit.json openmed audit status Show the audit configuration openmed audit disable Disable audit writes without deleting config openmed audit pause / resume Temporarily pause or resume audit writes openmed audit verify Smoke-test the configured destination openmed audit show --last N List recent traces openmed audit show <run_id> Print one trace JSON openmed audit export <run_id> Write one trace to a local JSON file openmed audit open Print the audit destination URL openmed audit set-phi-payload <mode> Set the payload mode: none, fingerprint, preview, or payload openmed audit set-flush-mode <mode> Set when traces are written: per_run or manual openmed audit local-list List local fallback traces openmed audit local-sync Push local fallback traces to the configured HF dataset

Default audit mode stores full private transcript and tool payloads. Use openmed audit set-phi-payload preview, fingerprint, or none for smaller records. See Audit Trail.

docs.title: Deterministic workflows
docs.text:
OpenMed ships 15 deterministic workflows. You normally invoke them through natural language in the TUI or inspect them with /workflows.

Workflow ID Purpose Required inputs appeal_review Review denied appeals against evidence requirements note_paths, denial_codes, procedure_cpt chart_summary Build evidence-linked chart summary cards and artifacts note_path claims_explainer Explain FHIR EOB data in plain language eob_path clinical_inbox_triage Triage patient message threads into urgent, routine, or admin routing with reply drafts thread_path clinical_documentation Convert visit transcripts into structured clinical notes note_path clinical_literature_research Research a topic across PubMed and MedlinePlus and produce a cited brief topic coding_audit Audit submitted ICD-10 codes for specificity and compliance submitted_codes_path, note_paths consumer_summary Summarize normalized consumer record imports with timeline, trends, questions, narrative, and reconciliation notes records_path or manifest_path discharge_handoff Build patient instructions, clinician summary, PCP handoff, and follow-up tasks from a discharge pack discharge_path health_summary Parse Apple Health data, analyze trends, and emit FHIR output health_export_path icd10_hcc_coding Build a coding package with validation, mappings, and claims context note_paths, submitted_codes_path med_rec_discrepancy Detect medication reconciliation discrepancies note_path prior_auth_review Review prior auth requests against codes and LCD/NCD criteria note_paths, procedure_cpt, diagnosis_icd10 special_pathogen_workup Build a reviewer-gated returned-traveler packet from CDC, WHO, PubMed, and MedlinePlus evidence case_text structured_extraction_fhir_diff Extract entities, build a FHIR bundle, and diff it note_paths

Common workflow behavior:

  • All 15 support draft preview
  • Models create drafts only. The TUI classifies each request as draft or finalized delivery with a small auxiliary model on your configured provider: explicit finalized requests are committed from the exact immutable snapshot in the same run; explicit draft requests and requests with no delivery wording stop at the draft. Natural follow-ups can approve an active draft without a run ID. The host still supplies a one-use exact-payload grant, and snapshots expire after 24 hours by default
  • Final output directories must be new, empty, or an existing OpenMed-owned bundle for the same workflow; unsafe or arbitrary nonempty destinations are rejected before finalization
  • clinical_inbox_triage and discharge_handoff also require real review_metadata at final write; the UI collects it when needed
  • consumer_summary, clinical_inbox_triage, and discharge_handoff are local review/generation flows; there is no outbound send or external-system writeback path in these lanes
  • Finalized runs write provenance data
  • Case runs can be listed and diffed through the workflow tool surface

Default output roots:

  • Artifacts: /tmp/openmed/artifacts/
  • Case runs: /tmp/openmed/cases/

Override them with OPENMED_WORKFLOW_ARTIFACTS_DIR and OPENMED_WORKFLOW_CASES_DIR. If the chosen root is not writable, OpenMed falls back to ./artifacts and ./cases in the working directory.

docs.text:
openmed config show
openmed config set timeout 600
openmed config profiles
openmed config profile-show dev
openmed config profile-use prod
openmed config profile-save myprofile
openmed config profile-delete myprofile

These commands manage the general CLI config file. The agent does not read its values; see General CLI config and Profiles.

docs.title: MCP management
docs.text:
openmed mcp list
openmed mcp add guidelines_hub https://example.com/mcp --name "Guidelines Hub"
openmed mcp enable guidelines_hub
openmed mcp enable --all
openmed mcp disable guidelines_hub
openmed mcp disable --all
openmed mcp set-url guidelines_hub https://new-url.example.com/mcp
openmed mcp remove guidelines_hub
openmed mcp doctor guidelines_hub
