MCP is the extension surface for remote systems that OpenMed does not already ship natively.

docs.title: Updates and diagnostics
docs.text:
openmed update
openmed update --check
openmed env
openmed env service-auth

1.0 is the final release line. On an older 1.0.x install, openmed update installs the final 1.0.x update; on the latest one it reports Already up to date. --check only checks and never installs; --force bypasses the cached version lookup.

openmed env is the quickest way to capture local environment details for debugging. openmed env service-auth checks that this install can authenticate to the hosted medical services; --audience narrows the check to inference, med_codes, or assets (default all).

docs.title: Clinical NLP
docs.text:
Turn a clinical note into a redaction draft you can inspect, process a collection of records, or extract clinical entities into files for further review. OpenMed Agent provides language and redaction controls, document previews, resumable batches, and extraction exports.

Clinical tools use your configured NLP service. With the hosted service, source content is processed remotely even when your chat model runs locally. De-identification is automated and can miss identifiers. Start with synthetic examples and review every result before sharing it.

docs.title: Start with a note
docs.text:
Open /privacy to select a source file and a new output path. Choose the language, redaction method, identifier categories, and whether to redact patient details, clinician details, or both. The review screen requires FULL PHI mode; use /phi to select it. The screen does not change this setting for you.

Select Allow an unqualified draft for my review if the request needs a review draft, then select Preview. For text output, Save shown output saves the preview you reviewed. Changing a control clears the old preview. You can cancel a request before saving, and the source file is preserved.

You can also describe the task in chat. Replace the example paths with your own:

Deidentify /path/cardiology.txt into /path/cardiology.masked.txt.
Use German and mask patient and clinician names, identifiers, phones,
email addresses, addresses and dates of birth. Preserve clinical terms,
diagnoses, medications and negation. I want a draft to review before saving.

For dedicated file redaction, provide the path directly. Reading or pasting the source into chat first can disclose it to the chat model. The dedicated file tools process the source through the NLP service and report a summary and output path; the review preview is displayed separately from the conversation.

docs.title: When a request needs review
docs.text:
A request can stop with “This request requires explicit review” and write nothing. The service gates output by language, model qualification and policy controls, so this is not only a language error, and switching language does not qualify the result. PDF and image input always needs a review draft.

To get a draft, opt in yourself:

  • In /privacy or /privacy-batch, select Allow an unqualified draft for my review and try again.
  • In chat, ask for a draft to review. OpenMed shows a dialog for that request. The model cannot answer it for you, and auto-approval does not cover it.
  • Headless openmed agent --once cannot show that dialog, so the request stops with no output. Use the TUI.

docs.title: Language and clinical preservation
docs.text:
Use automatic language selection or specify a language/locale such as en, de, DE or de-DE. In a prompt, “language German” is sufficient to request the language control. Text is not translated.

The clinical redaction profile is designed to preserve medical terms, diagnoses, medications, doses, units and negation while transforming selected identifiers. It distinguishes dates of birth from other dates: when birth dates are selected for redaction, the full birth date is removed rather than retaining its year.

Language controls do not establish accuracy for every language or national identifier. Availability depends on the configured service and model. Treat English and German results as drafts requiring review; do not assume that accepting a locale means every local identifier is covered. A higher detection threshold can leave more identifiers visible.

docs.title: Choose what to redact and preserve
docs.text:
Select patient details, clinician details, or both. For example, request patient-only redaction when the clinician's attribution needs to remain visible.

Available categories are person names, identifiers, phones, email addresses, addresses, dates of birth, other dates, URLs and organizations. In /privacy, other dates and organizations start unselected. Review the chosen categories before processing; keeping a category can leave identifying data.

For finer control in chat, request exact terms to preserve or label exceptions. The de-identification tool supports keep_terms and keep_labels. These advanced options are supplied through the prompt; the /privacy screen offers role and category controls, not a term-list editor.

Mask patient and clinician identifiers in /path/note.txt and write a review
draft to /path/note.masked.txt. Use language de. Keep the exact clinical
terms "Sozialanamnese" and "Kurznarkose". Show me the result before saving.

Term and label exceptions narrow redaction and require review. A term that also appears as an identifier can conflict with the requested policy. Inspect both what was removed and what remains.

docs.title: Five redaction methods
docs.text:
Method What to request What to expect mask Replace selected identifiers with labels Placeholders such as [TYPE] remove Delete selected identifiers Text with those spans removed replace Substitute fictional details Localized replacements where supported hash Use consistent pseudonyms within a named scope Repeatable replacements for the same identifier and scope; requires service support shift_dates Move dates by a specified number of days Shifted dates while preserving their intervals; selected birth dates are fully redacted

For hashing, choose a stable, non-identifying scope such as synthetic-study-a. Consistent pseudonyms allow records to remain linkable; they are not a guarantee of anonymity. Do not use a patient identifier as the scope.

For date shifting, supply a nonzero offset, for example:

Deidentify /path/note.txt into /path/note.shifted.txt using shift_dates.
Shift encounter dates by 30 days and fully redact dates of birth.
I want a draft for review.

The configured service determines which methods are available. PDF and image mask exports require mask; the other methods apply to text output.

docs.title: PDF and image redaction
docs.text:
The document preview supports PDF, PNG and JPEG input when enabled by your NLP service. In /privacy, choose OCR languages separately from the redaction language. The preview provides English, German, or both OCR packs.

Input Available output PDF OCR text draft, or a PDF mask draft PNG or JPEG OCR text draft, or a PNG mask draft

The on-screen preview shows OCR text. For PDF or PNG output, choose the matching output format, select Save review draft, then select Open saved file to inspect the actual masked pages alongside the source. PDF mask drafts are image-only documents; they do not retain the original searchable text layer.

The preview accepts up to eight pages and 8 MB per document, with additional image and recognized-text limits. OCR can miss or alter text. Check every page, including regions where OCR found nothing, before sharing an export.

docs.title: Long notes and resumable batches
docs.text:
Single-text redaction accepts up to 100,000 characters. The general read_file tool refuses files over 10 MB, which is a separate limit for files read into the conversation. Larger collections can use /privacy-batch for UTF-8 text, CSV or JSONL. Choose the source, output, checkpoint and selected text field, then set the redaction controls and review option. The batch screen also requires FULL PHI mode.

For example:

Deidentify the clinical_text column of /path/notes.csv into
/path/notes.masked.csv. Save the checkpoint at /path/notes.batch.json.
Use German, mask patient and clinician identifiers, and create drafts
for my review.

Follow progress and per-record status, cancel when needed, and resume with the same source, output, checkpoint and controls. Completed rows are retained. Keep these files together and unchanged between runs. Resume checks for changes so a different input is not silently treated as the original batch.

Limits are 1,000 records, 20 MB per source and 100,000 characters per selected field. Only the selected field is transformed. Other columns are preserved and may still contain identifiers. Failed or pending selected fields are blank; inspect row status before using the output.

docs.title: Clinical extraction and exports
docs.text:
Ask for disease, medication, anatomy, oncology, genomic or chemical entities from a note using the extraction tools. You can process one file or a collection and save structured results as JSONL.

Exports can select a particular extraction result. This helps with several notes or entity types: the saved file can refer to the intended extraction instead of relying only on whichever result ran last. A failed extraction does not leave an earlier result looking like its output.

Extract diseases and medications from /path/note.txt. Save each extraction
to its own JSONL file and read both files back to confirm what was written.

The language controls above apply to redaction, not to these entity extractors, and their accuracy is not established for every language. Extracted mentions are candidates for review, not confirmed diagnoses or prescribing instructions. Check doses, units, negation and whose history a mention describes against the source.

The chat model sees a small sample of extracted entities, and it sees any text placed in the conversation. Use the dedicated redaction tools when the source should stay out of the chat.

docs.title: File privacy controls
docs.text:
File privacy is off by default. Choose a mode explicitly:

Command Behavior /privacy-chat off Use the usual tools permitted by the session's other settings /privacy-chat on Restrict subsequent file work to the dedicated privacy tools /privacy-chat auto Wait for a recognized file-redaction request, then activate the restriction

The selected mode survives session resume. Once auto activates, it stays active until you select off or reset it to auto. Automatic recognition does not cover every language or phrasing; use on when you want the restriction immediately. Stop or finish an active turn before changing modes. For headless runs, pass --file-privacy off, on or auto with openmed agent --once.

These controls do not scrub text already pasted into chat or make hosted NLP processing local. PHI mode is a separate setting. See Privacy & Security for detailed behavior.

docs.title: Installation and setup
docs.text: For installation and provider setup, see Getting Started and Providers.

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: OpenMed configuration spans local config files, auth files, session storage, workflow output directories, and environment variables.

docs.title: Files And Directories
docs.text:
Path Purpose ~/.openmed/provider_secrets.json Optional per-user OpenAI / Anthropic / OpenRouter / MiMo / Doubleword API keys created by openmed config provider-set ~/.openmed/auth.json Credential file for the experimental ChatGPT sign-in, created by openmed login ~/.openmed/audit.json Optional private audit-trail destination and PHI payload policy ~/.openmed/traces/ Local audit trace store and HF-write fallback path ~/.openmed/service_secrets.json Optional endpoints and keys for your own medical service planes ~/.openmed/sessions/ Persisted TUI session data ~/.openmed/history.jsonl Local prompt history for Up/Down recall (last 100 entries, skipped in DEID mode) ~/.config/openmed/config.toml General CLI configuration ~/.config/openmed/profiles/ Custom configuration profiles ~/.config/openmed/skills/ User-installed local skills ~/.config/openmed/mcp_servers.json MCP server configuration ~/.config/openmed/mcp_tools_cache.json Cached MCP tool discovery results ~/.openmed/cache/openrouter_models.json Cached OpenRouter model capability metadata (24h) ~/.openmed/batches/<job-id>/ Private Doubleword batch state, staged input, partial output, and error JSONL ~/.openmed/responses/<response-id>.json Private Doubleword flex/priority request and result snapshots; override with OPENMED_RESPONSES_DIR ./.openmed/OPENMED_PLAN.md Human-readable durable global plan for long workspace-scoped runs ./.openmed/OPENMED_PLAN.json Machine-readable durable global plan ledger and validation state /tmp/openmed/artifacts/ Default workflow artifact root /tmp/openmed/cases/ Default case-run root

~/.config follows XDG_CONFIG_HOME when that variable is set.

docs.title: General CLI Config
docs.text:
~/.config/openmed/config.toml holds the keys that openmed config show, openmed config set, and profiles manage. OpenMed creates it the first time you save a value:

# OpenMed configuration file
# Generated automatically. Edit with care.

default_org = "OpenMed"
cache_dir = "/home/you/.cache/openmed"
device = null
hf_token = null
log_level = "INFO"
timeout = 300
use_medical_tokenizer = true
medical_tokenizer_exceptions = null
profile = null

The TUI and openmed agent --once do not read these values. To change how the agent runs, use the runtime settings below.

OpenMed writes this file so that only you can read it, and it never copies HF_TOKEN from the environment into it. A token you set yourself with openmed config set hf_token is stored here as plain text.

docs.title: Runtime Settings
docs.text:
OpenMed loads per-project and per-user runtime settings that control permission policy, tool filtering, and result persistence. These are separate from the general CLI config and profiles.

Path Purpose ./OPENMED.md Project instructions injected into the system prompt (loaded from the git root, or the working directory outside a git repository) ./.openmed/settings.json Project-level runtime settings (same location rule) ~/.openmed/settings.json User-level runtime settings

Settings cascade: CLI arguments > project settings > user settings > defaults. Each key resolves on its own, and a project list replaces the user list instead of merging with it.

A settings file looks like this:

{
  "permission_mode": "auto",
  "deny_tools": ["edit_*"],
  "ask_tools": ["write_file"],
  "tool_result_persist_threshold_chars": 50000,
  "model": "gpt-6.1-sol",
  "provider": "openai",
  "reasoning_effort": "medium"
}

Supported runtime settings keys:

Key Type Default Purpose permission_mode auto / acceptall / denyall / plan auto Tool execution gating mode allow_tools list of tool name patterns none Strict allowlist: when set, the model sees only matching tools, and they run without a prompt. Ignored in the consumer and coordination agent modes, which have their own lists deny_tools list of tool name patterns none Tools removed entirely ask_tools list of tool name patterns none Tools that always prompt for approval tool_result_persist_threshold_chars integer 50000 Oversized results written to disk above this threshold model model ID built-in default Default model for new sessions (openmed config model-set) provider openai / anthropic / openrouter / mimo / doubleword / custom inferred from the model Provider for the saved model reasoning_effort none / low / medium / high / xhigh / max medium Default reasoning effort

deny_tools and ask_tools accept shell-style wildcards such as edit_*. allow_tools accepts exact tool names and a trailing *, such as read_*.

model, provider, and reasoning_effort apply when OpenMed starts; see Default model and newer models. model and provider are read as a pair, so a project model is never combined with the user's provider.

The model picker also stores its favorites and recents here, under a model_prefs key that it manages itself.

In acceptall, ask_tools does not trigger per-call approval prompts; use deny_tools to block tools that should never run in full-access mode.

Use /config in the TUI to see the effective runtime configuration at any time.

docs.title: Core Environment Variables
docs.text:
Provider credentials and provider-specific tuning (OPENAI_API_KEY, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENROUTER_*, MIMO_API_KEY, DOUBLEWORD_API_KEY, OPENMED_ANTHROPIC_*) are documented on the Providers page.

Variable Purpose Default / behavior OPENMED_HOME Override the ~/.openmed root used for global auth and sessions ~/.openmed OPENMED_CONFIG Override the config file path (--config-path does the same for one command) ~/.config/openmed/config.toml OPENMED_PROFILE Name the active config profile when the config file has none. Does not load the profile's values unset OPENMED_PROVIDER_SECRETS_PATH Override the provider secrets file path ~/.openmed/provider_secrets.json OPENMED_WORKFLOW_ARTIFACTS_DIR Override workflow artifact root /tmp/openmed/artifacts OPENMED_WORKFLOW_CASES_DIR Override case-run root /tmp/openmed/cases OPENMED_BATCH_DIR Override the private asynchronous batch job root ~/.openmed/batches OPENMED_RESPONSES_DIR Override private individual Responses request and result storage ~/.openmed/responses OPENMED_SKILLS_DIR Override the user skills directory ~/.config/openmed/skills OPENMED_DRAFT_SNAPSHOT_TTL_SECONDS Lifetime of immutable workflow draft snapshots 86400 (24 hours) OPENMED_AUTO_APPROVE Skip tool approval prompts and log each one (1, true, yes, or on) off OPENMED_NO_UPDATE_CHECK Skip the background release check at TUI startup (1, true, yes, or on) off

docs.title: Audit And Trace Storage
docs.text:
Audit trails are off by default. When enabled, OpenMed writes one JSON trace per agent run to a private destination owned by the operator.

Supported destinations:

  • hf_dataset — private Hugging Face Dataset repo, recommended for versioned audit history
  • hf_bucket — private Hugging Face Storage Bucket
  • local — local JSON traces only

Enable a private dataset destination:

export OPENMED_AUDIT_HF_TOKEN=hf_...
openmed audit enable --destination hf_dataset --dataset "<user-or-org>/openmed-traces"

This writes ~/.openmed/audit.json:

{
  "enabled": true,
  "schema_version": "1.0",
  "destination": "hf_dataset",
  "phi_payload": "payload",
  "flush_mode": "per_run",
  "local": {
    "path": "~/.openmed/traces",
    "fallback_on_hf_failure": true
  },
  "hf": {
    "repo": "<user-or-org>/openmed-traces",
    "token_env": "OPENMED_AUDIT_HF_TOKEN"
  }
}

Environment variables override this file:

Variable Purpose Default OPENMED_AUDIT_CONFIG_PATH Override the audit config file path ~/.openmed/audit.json OPENMED_AUDIT_ENABLED Override audit on/off at runtime config file / off OPENMED_AUDIT_DESTINATION hf_dataset, hf_bucket, local, or none config file / none OPENMED_AUDIT_HF_TOKEN HF token for private audit writes token_env, then HF_TOKEN, if present OPENMED_AUDIT_HF_REPO Target private HF dataset repo config file OPENMED_AUDIT_HF_BUCKET Target private HF bucket config file OPENMED_AUDIT_PHI_PAYLOAD none, fingerprint, preview, or payload payload OPENMED_AUDIT_FLUSH_MODE per_run or manual per_run OPENMED_AUDIT_LOCAL_FALLBACK Write local trace if HF write fails 1 OPENMED_AUDIT_LOCAL_PATH Local audit trace path ~/.openmed/traces

Default phi_payload=payload stores full private transcript and tool payloads. Use preview, fingerprint, or none for smaller traces. See Audit Trail for the trace schema and CLI commands.

docs.title: Model Providers
docs.text:
Credentials, model selection, and per-provider behaviour for OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter, MiMo, Doubleword, and custom endpoints are documented together on the Providers page.

See Providers for API keys and ~/.openmed/provider_secrets.json, the experimental ChatGPT sign-in, OpenRouter models, MiMo setup, Anthropic caching, and provider selection. See Doubleword for real-time, async Responses and batch mode selection, and Batch Inference for bulk job storage and resume behavior.

docs.title: Doubleword credentials and execution mode
docs.text:
Store the key once with openmed config provider-set doubleword --api-key "sk-...", or export DOUBLEWORD_API_KEY. The stored location is provider.doubleword.options.apiKey inside ~/.openmed/provider_secrets.json. An optional models list beside apiKey customizes the picker and makes its first entry the interactive default; DOUBLEWORD_MODELS overrides it. See Doubleword model configuration. No base URL or async flag belongs in that entry:

{
  "provider": {
    "doubleword": {
      "options": {
        "apiKey": "sk-...",
        "models": ["deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash"]
      }
    }
  }
}

Select the mode when running a command: openmed agent --provider doubleword starts the real-time TUI; openmed responses submit request.json --service-tier flex submits an individual async request; openmed batch submit requests.jsonl submits a 24-hour bulk job. --wait only keeps the local command polling. It does not change the tier, price, or completion window. See the complete setup and request example.

docs.title: MiMo credentials example
docs.text:
MiMo token-plan users can configure just the key in ~/.openmed/provider_secrets.json:

{
  "provider": {
    "mimo": {
      "options": {
        "apiKey": "tp-..."
      }
    }
  }
}

Replace the placeholder with your token-plan key, or use "{env:MIMO_API_KEY}" and export that variable. Add mimo inside the existing provider object if you already have other providers configured. Then run openmed agent --provider mimo; the endpoint and all four model names are built in. See MiMo provider configuration for key precedence, model selection, and troubleshooting. Keep API keys out of settings.json and project files.

docs.title: Context And Compaction
docs.text: OpenMed sends its full tool schema (about 23,000 tokens) plus the system prompt on every turn, so expect more than 25,000 tokens of fixed overhead before any patient content. Long sessions therefore need compaction: older turns are summarized so the request keeps fitting.

docs.title: How OpenMed decides when to compact
docs.text:
Compaction runs when the estimated request crosses a fraction of the model's context window (0.80 by default, lower for some models, such as 0.70 on GPT-6). That requires knowing the window, which OpenMed resolves in this order:

Provider Source of the window OpenAI / Codex / Anthropic / MiMo V2.5 Curated per-model table OpenRouter The model's own metadata, using the window the routed provider actually serves (not the model's theoretical maximum, which can be several times larger) Doubleword Curated serving windows from Doubleword's Models dashboard and documentation, scoped to this provider and the exact model alias Custom endpoint The server's own /models listing (max_model_len), read at startup Anything else Unknown

OpenMed has no context window for the MiMo V2.6 IDs, so it leaves proactive compaction off for them and relies on the reactive overflow recovery path.

Doubleword's 11 built-in models have known windows: 1,000,000 tokens for the DeepSeek, GLM, Kimi K3 and Inkling entries; a conservative 262,000 tokens for Kimi K2.6 and both Nemotron entries. These are built into OpenMed and use the dashboard's rounded serving limits; OpenMed does not read a window from Doubleword's /v1/models listing. Any other model ID on Doubleword, such as an account-specific alias, has an unknown window.

At the default 80% threshold, the 1M models compact near 800K request tokens, including the SDK's reserved output budget. A 28K request is not near that threshold. To choose 50% instead, launch with OPENMED_COMPACTION_THRESHOLD=0.5 openmed agent --provider doubleword. This changes the compaction threshold, not the model's actual window.

An unknown window disables automatic compaction

OpenMed does not guess a context window. If it cannot determine one, it turns proactive compaction off rather than compact against a fabricated number — summarizing is lossy and irreversible, and in a clinical session the transcript is the record. You will see a one-time notice in the TUI, and /compact remains available to compact manually.

A guessed window is wrong in both directions: too small and OpenMed compacts a session that had plenty of room; too large and it never compacts until the server errors.

Compaction still runs reactively in all cases: when a provider reports that the request no longer fits, OpenMed compacts once and retries. Rate limits are explicitly not treated as overflow, so a throttle never destroys history.

docs.title: Making an unknown window known
docs.text:
For a self-hosted or custom endpoint, run the doctor:

openmed config endpoint-doctor http://localhost:8000/v1

vLLM and SGLang report max_model_len on /v1/models, which the doctor reads directly. If your server does not report a window, the doctor fails the context check and tells you what to set.

docs.title: Silent truncation
docs.text:
Some servers do not error when a prompt exceeds their context — they drop the front of it. The front is exactly where OpenMed's system prompt and tool schemas live, so the symptom is a model that appears to ignore its instructions and refuses to call tools, with nothing in any log. llama.cpp defaults to a 4096-token context, and Ollama's default auto-scales with available VRAM and can land at 4k.

endpoint-doctor detects this with a canary: it places a unique token at the very start of the system prompt, pads to the size of a real turn, and asks the model to echo it back. If the token comes back, the front survived.

  [FAIL] truncation: The model could not see a token placed at the START of the
         system prompt, and the server returned no error — it is silently
         truncating.

A server that errors on an over-long prompt passes this check — refusing is the honest behaviour.

docs.title: Setting context explicitly on your server
docs.text: Engine Flag Default if unset vLLM --max-model-len 65536 The model's maximum (can OOM the KV cache) SGLang --context-length 65536 The model's maximum llama.cpp --ctx-size 65536 4096 — truncates every turn Ollama OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH=65536 before ollama serve Auto-scales; can be 4k. Verify with ollama ps Variable Purpose Default OPENMED_COMPACTION_THRESHOLD Override the fraction of the window at which compaction triggers. Clamped to 0.10–0.95 per-model, 0.80 unless the model sets a lower value

docs.title: Web Search
docs.text:
Web search is off by default on every provider, including OpenAI and ChatGPT OAuth. Enabling it sends queries — which may contain clinical detail — to a third-party search vendor, so it is an explicit operator decision. Full setup and privacy guidance: Web Search.

export OPENMED_WEB_SEARCH=1
export SERPER_API_KEY="..."       # or TAVILY_API_KEY / BRAVE_SEARCH_API_KEY

Both parts are required: a key alone does nothing, so adding one for another purpose can never silently start sending clinical queries.

When search has never been enabled the search_web tool is hidden from the model entirely, so it does not spend schema budget on a capability that cannot work. If you enable search but the backend is misconfigured, the tool stays visible and explains exactly what is wrong.

docs.title: Provider-native search (OpenAI and Codex OAuth)
docs.text:
OpenAI's Responses API — used by both the OpenAI provider and ChatGPT OAuth — can run a server-side search where the model searches and returns prose. OpenMed does not request it by default, for two reasons: it is unavailable on Anthropic, OpenRouter and local models, so behaviour would differ by provider; and its results never reach OpenMed as inspectable sources, so a claim drawn from them cannot be traced to a page you can open.

If you accept that trade — for non-clinical research use, for example — enable it per session:

Variable Purpose Default OPENMED_BUILTIN_WEB_SEARCH Request the provider's server-side web_search tool on OpenAI / Codex OAuth 0 (off) 
OPENMED_BUILTIN_WEB_SEARCH=1 openmed agent --model gpt-6.1-sol

This is independent of OPENMED_WEB_SEARCH: the two can be used together, and the client-side tool is the one that produces citable sources.

docs.title: Native Medical Services
docs.text:
OpenMed ships native medical tools, but many of them use OpenMed's native medical service plane rather than an embedded local model binary.

These are native OpenMed tools. They are not remote MCP servers.

The service split is intentional:

  • extraction and de-identification run on a dedicated native service plane
  • terminology, HCC, RAF, RxNorm, LOINC, MedlinePlus, and PubMed run on a dedicated native service plane

The point of that split is not locality for its own sake. It is to keep sensitive or high-volume clinical processing on dedicated service planes that are easier to govern, faster on long unstructured inputs, and more cost-efficient than routing every page through a frontier-model path. General agent reasoning still uses the configured model provider.

By default, OpenMed operates these native medical services. To point either service plane at your own server, set OPENMED_INFERENCE_URL / OPENMED_MED_CODES_API_URL or use ~/.openmed/service_secrets.json:

{
  "inference": {
    "base_url": "https://nlp.internal.example.org",
    "api_key": "{env:OPENMED_NLP_KEY}"
  },
  "med_codes": {
    "base_url": "https://codes.internal.example.org",
    "api_key": "{env:OPENMED_CODES_KEY}"
  }
}

Every field is optional. See Use your own service endpoints for all fields.

See Native Medical Services for the deployment story and hosting patterns.

docs.title: MCP Configuration
docs.text:
~/.config/openmed/mcp_servers.json lists your remote MCP servers:

{
  "version": 1,
  "servers": [
    {
      "id": "guidelines_hub",
      "name": "Guidelines Hub",
      "url": "https://example.com/mcp",
      "enabled": true,
      "timeout_seconds": 20,
      "extra_headers": {}
    }
  ]
}

See MCP Connectors for the validation rules.

Variable Purpose Default OPENMED_MCP_CONFIG_PATH Override MCP config file path ~/.config/openmed/mcp_servers.json OPENMED_MCP_TOOLS_CACHE_PATH Override tool-cache path ~/.config/openmed/mcp_tools_cache.json OPENMED_MCP_TOOLS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS Override discovery cache TTL 3600 OPENMED_MCP_<SERVER_ID>_ENABLED Override a server's enabled state unset OPENMED_MCP_<SERVER_ID>_URL Override a server's URL unset OPENMED_MCP_<SERVER_ID>_HEADERS_JSON Override a server's auth headers unset

docs.title: Session PHI Mode
docs.text:
OpenMed exposes a session PHI mode in the CLI/TUI:

  • full
  • deid
  • strict

This mode is stored in session state and shown in the UI. deid and strict restrict what can reach the model: tools that return raw record content and workflows that read local files are refused. See PHI modes for exactly what each mode enforces and its limits.

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text:
openmed config profiles
openmed config profile-show dev
openmed config profile-use prod

See Profiles for built-in and custom profile details.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text: OpenMed Agent is closed source and ships only as a signed binary. Version 1.0 is the final release line: no further versions are planned after the last 1.0.x maintenance update, and OpenMed does not accept code contributions.

docs.title: Reporting a problem
docs.text:
Send bug reports to support@openmed.life; see Support. Because no further versions are planned, a report is unlikely to lead to a fix in the binary.

openmed env prints the version, configuration paths, provider status, and service endpoints in use. It is usually enough to diagnose a local configuration problem yourself, and it is useful to include in a report:

openmed env

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Get from zero to a running OpenMed agent in a few minutes.

docs.title: 1. Install
docs.text:
curl -fsSL "<your install.sh URL>" | bash

This places the OpenMed binary on your machine and sets up the openmed command. Binaries are published for macOS on Apple silicon (arm64) and Linux x64 (glibc).

Your install link is sent with your access invitation. If you do not have one yet, request access.

docs.title: 2. Authenticate
docs.text:
OpenAI API keyAnthropic API keyOpenRouter API keyMiMo token planDoublewordChatGPT sign-in (experimental)

The recommended way to use OpenAI models. Store a provider key:

openmed config provider-set openai --api-key "sk-..."
openmed config provider-show

You can also use an environment variable or an environment reference in ~/.openmed/provider_secrets.json:

export OPENAI_API_KEY=sk-...

No openmed login step is required in that case.

To use Anthropic models, store an Anthropic provider key:

openmed config provider-set anthropic --api-key "sk-ant-..."
openmed config provider-show

You can also use an environment variable or an environment reference in ~/.openmed/provider_secrets.json:

export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=sk-ant-...

With only an Anthropic key, plain openmed starts on claude-sonnet-4-6. To always use another Claude model, save it as your default:

openmed config model-set claude-opus-5-5 --provider anthropic

You can also choose a Claude model in the TUI model picker, or launch with an explicit provider/model pair:

openmed agent --provider anthropic --model claude-sonnet-4-6

To use models from other vendors through one key, store an OpenRouter key:

openmed config provider-set openrouter --api-key "sk-or-..."

Or use an environment variable:

export OPENROUTER_API_KEY=sk-or-...

Then launch on OpenRouter:

openmed agent --provider openrouter

Choose which models appear in the /model picker:

openmed config provider-set openrouter \
  --models "qwen/qwen3.8-27b,z-ai/glm-5.2"

Without a configured model list, qwen/qwen3.8-27b is the OpenRouter default. Browse the catalog with openmed config openrouter-models. OpenMed only accepts models that support tool calling, and does not evaluate the OpenRouter catalog — see Providers for model examples and the caveats that matter for clinical use.

Store the tp key from your Xiaomi MiMo token-plan subscription:

openmed config provider-set mimo --api-key "tp-..."
openmed agent --provider mimo

Or export MIMO_API_KEY="tp-..." before launching. No openmed login, base URL, or model list is required. The default is mimo-v2.5-pro; select any of the other built-in models with /model, or at launch:

openmed agent --provider mimo --model mimo-v2.6-pro
openmed agent --provider mimo --model mimo-v2.6-flash

Token-plan keys use the Amsterdam endpoint automatically. Pay-as-you-go sk keys are not supported. See the complete provider secrets examples.

Store one key for real-time, async and batch inference:

openmed config provider-set doubleword --api-key "sk-..."
openmed config provider-show

Or export DOUBLEWORD_API_KEY="sk-...". Start a real-time TUI session with:

openmed agent --provider doubleword

The picker includes 11 generation models, starting with DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. An optional provider models list replaces those defaults; its first entry becomes the launch model.

Async is a separate CLI workflow, not a provider-secret setting or TUI toggle. Follow the three-mode quickstart for complete, copyable examples. Create the example request JSON, then run openmed responses submit request.json --service-tier flex. Submission returns an ID to poll or resume later. For independent overnight work, prepare a batch JSONL file and use openmed batch submit requests.jsonl instead. See Doubleword for setup, modes and the data boundary.

Experimental

ChatGPT sign-in is not an officially supported OpenAI API integration and can stop working without notice. Use an OpenAI API key for anything you depend on.

Uses your ChatGPT subscription through a browser sign-in:

openmed login

This writes credentials to ~/.openmed/auth.json. OpenMed uses this single file from every project.

Provider keys vs native medical services

OpenAI, Anthropic, OpenRouter, MiMo and Doubleword keys authenticate model inference. Native medical services are a separate OpenMed service plane.

Standard binaries use OpenMed's native medical services without additional local service setup. To use your own servers instead, see Native Medical Services.

When multiple providers are configured

Claude models route to Anthropic. GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 models route to ChatGPT sign-in first when ~/.openmed/auth.json exists, then to the OpenAI provider key (use --provider openai to choose the key). Explicit GPT-5.5 selections run on the OpenAI API and need an API key. Namespaced ids such as qwen/qwen3.8-27b route to OpenRouter. Bare mimo-v2.5-pro, mimo-v2.5, mimo-v2.6-pro, and mimo-v2.6-flash IDs use MiMo token-plan credentials. Full details on the Providers page. For Doubleword, pass --provider doubleword explicitly, particularly with namespaced model IDs that OpenRouter also serves.

docs.title: 3. Launch the agent
docs.text:
openmed

That starts the interactive TUI.

To launch with a specific model or inspect the model catalog:

openmed --model gpt-6.1-sol
openmed --model gpt-6-luna
openmed --models

By default the app launches with gpt-6.1-sol and medium reasoning, unless you saved another default with openmed config model-set:

  • With an OpenAI provider key, it runs on your OpenAI key. If ChatGPT sign-in credentials (experimental) are also present, sign-in is used first; add --provider openai to use the key.
  • With credentials only for other providers (Anthropic, OpenRouter, MiMo, Doubleword, or a custom endpoint), OpenMed uses that provider's default model and says so in the session. Use --provider when choosing one of them alongside other configured providers.
  • With no credentials at all, the TUI opens and tells you what to set. Add a key in another terminal; your next message picks it up.

The built-in agent modes are:

  • clinical — the default full clinical and operational lane
  • consumer — restricted personal-health workflows for imports, trends, summaries, and visit prep
  • coordination — restricted inbox/discharge lane for reviewer-safe patient-facing drafts

Agent modes set the lane. To explore without changing anything, switch the TUI to the read-only access mode with /access.

docs.title: Clinical extraction
docs.text:
Type a natural-language request in the input box:

Extract diseases and medications from this text and save to /tmp/entities.jsonl:
The patient is a 65-year-old male with Type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypertension,
and chronic kidney disease stage 3. Currently taking metformin 1000mg BID and
lisinopril 10mg daily.

A successful run typically looks like this:

  1. OpenMed creates a plan
  2. It calls extract_entities for the relevant entity types
  3. It saves structured output to the requested file
  4. It reports the result inline in the TUI

docs.title: Consumer health summary
docs.text:
Launch the restricted consumer lane:

openmed agent --agent consumer --skill analyzing-health-data

Then ask for a multi-source summary:

Import this Health Connect export into /tmp/openmed-consumer-demo and run a draft consumer_summary with timeline, trends, visit-prep questions, reconciliation notes, and optional FHIR output:
@/path/to/health_connect_export.json

This lane is designed for personal-health record imports and summaries. It does not auto-send anything or write back into external systems.

docs.title: Care coordination
docs.text:
Launch the restricted coordination lane:

openmed agent --agent coordination --skill care-coordination

Then ask for a reviewer-safe draft:

Normalize this portal export into a message-thread pack and run a draft clinical_inbox_triage workflow with follow-up tasks and a constrained reply draft:
@/path/to/portal_export.json

Or use the discharge workflow:

Normalize this discharge export and run a draft discharge_handoff workflow with patient instructions, clinician summary, PCP handoff, and follow-up tasks:
@/path/to/discharge_export.json

Native medical tool services

The local runtime is only part of the system. Many medical capabilities call OpenMed's native medical service plane.

  • Extraction, PII, de-identification, terminology, HCC, RAF, and education tools are native OpenMed capabilities
  • Standard binaries use OpenMed-hosted native services without extra local setup
  • Each service plane can point at your own cloud, VPC, or on-prem server; see Native Medical Services
  • Consumer-import and care-coordination adapter flows remain local-only; there is no outbound send or external-system writeback path in those lanes

These are native OpenMed tools, not MCP servers.

docs.title: 5. Add remote MCP servers (optional)
docs.text:
Use MCP when you want tools that OpenMed does not already ship natively:

openmed mcp add guidelines_hub https://example.com/mcp --name "Guidelines Hub"
openmed mcp doctor guidelines_hub

Once added, remote MCP tools appear under the mcp__<server_id>__<tool> namespace and can be invoked by the agent like any other tool.

docs.title: 6. Know where review points appear
docs.text:
• Deterministic workflows always create an immutable draft first. Ask for finalized output and the host finalizes that exact snapshot in the same run; ask for a draft, or omit the delivery state, and the draft completes the plan. Later natural language such as “looks good, send it” works without a run ID. Questions, edits, negations, failures, and ambiguous targets fail closed
  • In the default Ask access mode, edit_file and any tool you list in ask_tools pause for an approval dialog on every provider. Other tools, including write_file, run without a prompt; see Permission policy
  • Normal read/search/extraction tool calls are still visible in the TUI even when they do not require a modal approval step

docs.title: 7. Enable audit traces (optional)
docs.text:
Audit is off by default. If you need a durable private record of runs, configure a private Hugging Face dataset or local-only trace store:

export OPENMED_AUDIT_HF_TOKEN=hf_...
openmed audit enable --destination hf_dataset --dataset "<user-or-org>/openmed-traces"
openmed audit status

The default audit mode stores full private transcript and tool payloads. Use openmed audit set-phi-payload preview, fingerprint, or none if you need a smaller audit record.

docs.title: Troubleshooting
docs.text:
Token expired or login fails

Re-run login:

openmed login -f

ChatGPT sign-in is experimental and can stop working if OpenAI changes it. An OpenAI API key is the supported alternative:

openmed config provider-set openai --api-key "sk-..."
openmed agent --provider openai
MiMo key or model is rejected

MiMo requires a token-plan key starting with tp and one of mimo-v2.5-pro, mimo-v2.5, mimo-v2.6-pro, or mimo-v2.6-flash. sk pay-as-you-go keys are not supported. Run openmed config provider-show to check whether the key is set without displaying it. See MiMo troubleshooting.

MiMo takes a long time to start streaming

Read the activity label first. Preparing request… means OpenMed has not started the primary stream yet. Waiting for model response… means it has dispatched the primary request and has not received a reasoning or answer delta. The direct token-plan endpoint and OpenRouter's xiaomi/... route are separate serving paths, so their first-token latency is not expected to match. See MiMo startup latency.

MCP server unreachable

Run the connectivity check:

openmed mcp doctor --all

Common causes: firewall rules, VPN routing, expired auth headers, or the remote endpoint not actually speaking JSON-RPC MCP.

Where are OAuth credentials stored?

openmed login writes only ~/.openmed/auth.json. OpenMed ignores a project-local ./auth.json.

docs.title: Run an agent workflow from the CLI
docs.text: openmed agent --once runs one request through the same provider SDK and tool bridge used by the TUI, then exits. It can extract entities, validate codes, call HCC services, and create draft reports. Use it for scripts, CI checks, and scheduled retrospective work that needs tools as well as a model answer.

docs.title: Start with one request
docs.text:
Configure a provider first. For example, use DOUBLEWORD_API_KEY or the existing Doubleword entry in ~/.openmed/provider_secrets.json. There is no separate headless credential.

openmed agent --provider doubleword \
  --model deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
  --once 'List the available deterministic workflows and explain which produces a coding audit draft.'

Omit --provider to resolve the model against configured authentication. With no explicit model, a default saved with openmed config model-set is used; otherwise an authenticated OpenAI/Codex default is preferred, then an available provider's recommended model. Explicit model/provider choices are not silently replaced. Configure a provider API key (or sign in with openmed login) beforehand; headless runs never open a sign-in dialog.

For longer prompts, redirect a file into stdin. This also avoids putting the prompt itself in a process argument:

openmed agent --provider doubleword --once - --json --timeout 600 \
  < prompt.txt > result.json 2> progress.log
status=$?

Normal stdout contains the final answer. --json instead emits one JSON object with schema_version, status, exit_code, provider, model, content, tool_calls, artifact_paths, approvals, errors, and provider-reported usage. Tool receipts include results and may contain source text or clinical data: keep them private. Progress and diagnostics go to stderr. Intermediate reasoning and pre-tool narration are not mixed into the final answer.

The command does not create or resume a TUI conversation. --session is rejected. An interrupted run cannot be resumed by ID; starting the command again performs new work and may repeat charges or side effects. Keep each run's outputs separate.

docs.title: Permissions and privacy
docs.text:
Project/user runtime settings and OPENMED.md apply, as do agent profile tool restrictions and --skill. Enabled remote MCP tools use the normal registry. The CLI does not bypass protected paths or host file-privacy restrictions.

  • Default approval behavior uses the configured tool policy. Ordinary permitted tools run; an operation requiring an interactive approval is denied.
  • --auto-approve (or OPENMED_AUTO_APPROVE=1) explicitly grants ordinary tool prompts and records each grant. Deny rules still apply. It never grants workflow finalization or clinical-review consent.
  • --permission-mode plan permits only tools marked both read-only and safe for concurrent use. denyall blocks tools; auto uses the normal permission rules. An explicit CLI mode overrides the stored mode, while allow/deny lists remain.
  • File writes already allowed by the policy can happen without a prompt. For a restricted script, configure an explicit tool allowlist and deny rules in runtime settings.
  • --file-privacy on restricts access to the dedicated privacy tools and metadata inspection. auto activates that restriction for recognized file-privacy requests; the default is off. This does not scrub text supplied in a prompt.
  • Headless runs support --phi-mode full only. deid and strict are rejected before any request is sent; use the TUI for those modes. Use synthetic or appropriately de-identified inputs.

A draft is not a clinical approval. Workflow finalization and clinical-review consent require the interactive host, even if the model supplies a token or review_mode=true.

docs.title: Exit codes
docs.text:
Code Meaning 0 Agent returned a final answer with no recorded tool failure or denied approval 1 Provider/runtime failure or termination without a final answer 2 Invalid configuration/input or unsupported option combination 3 Required interactive approval or clinical review was unavailable 4 At least one tool failed or was blocked by policy, even if the model later produced an answer 124 Timeout 130 Interrupted with Ctrl+C / SIGINT

Inspect receipts on any nonzero exit. A later successful retry does not erase an earlier tool failure. Exit zero means successful execution, not clinical correctness; validate the artifacts for your use case.

--timeout defaults to 600 seconds and cancels the run. The command exits with code 124 without waiting for a tool that is still running, so a call already in flight can be cut off or finish on the remote side. Completed file writes and remote effects are not rolled back. Provider clients are closed on exit.

docs.title: When to use batch instead
docs.text: --once is a real-time agent/tool loop. Doubleword responses and batch commands submit inference requests and do not execute returned tool calls. For a large backlog that can wait up to 24 hours, prepare deterministic NLP/coding evidence first, then use batch inference for independent model reviews. Dependent tool/model stages need orchestration; changing provider secrets does not turn --once into a background batch job.

docs.title: Long-Term Use
docs.text:
OpenMed Agent 1.0 is the final release line, and its last maintenance update has shipped. No further versions, fixes, or support are planned. On the latest 1.0.x release, openmed update reports that you are up to date. This page explains what that means in practice and how to keep working as the world around the software changes.

The terms are in the license, which you can read at any time with openmed --license.

docs.title: What stays the same
docs.text:
• The software on your machine. The installed binary has no expiry date, and your sessions, plans, skills, and settings stay in ~/.openmed/.
  • Your own providers. Your API keys talk directly to your model provider. As long as the provider serves a compatible API, OpenMed keeps working with it.
  • Your own services. Anything you point at your own servers, such as a custom model endpoint or your own medical service endpoints, depends only on those servers.

docs.title: What can change
docs.text:
OpenMed depends on things outside the binary. The table shows what to do when one of them changes.

What changes What you will see What to do A provider retires a model An error saying the model is unavailable, with a hint to pick another one Choose a newer model. See Default model and newer models A provider releases a newer model It is not in the /model list Pass its ID with --model, or add it to your list with openmed config provider-set ChatGPT sign-in stops working Sign-in or request errors Switch to an OpenAI API key. ChatGPT sign-in is experimental and can stop working at any time A provider changes its API Provider errors on every request Use another provider, or a custom endpoint that speaks the OpenAI-compatible API A hosted medical service is unavailable "Temporarily unavailable" errors, stopped reviews, or DEGRADED reports Try again later. See When a service is unavailable Hosted medical services are discontinued The same errors, and they do not clear See If hosted services go away Trusted certificates change, or your network inspects TLS Certificate errors on every connection Set SSL_CERT_FILE to a current CA bundle, for example export SSL_CERT_FILE=/path/to/ca-bundle.pem

Hosted services are provided as available and may change, be interrupted, or be discontinued.

docs.title: If hosted services go away
docs.text:
The agent, your model provider, local file tools, sessions, and your own skills do not need OpenMed-hosted services. These parts do:

Part Without hosted services Built-in skills Unavailable. They are delivered by the hosted service and are not stored in the binary Reference data for prior authorization and appeal reviews Unavailable. Those workflows stop with an error Coding and terminology tools, HCC, and RAF Unavailable, unless you point them at a compatible server you operate Extraction, PII detection, and de-identification Unavailable, unless you point them at a compatible server you operate. DEID mode depends on this service

Your own skills keep working, and MCP connectors can supply your own medical tools.

docs.title: Clinical reference data ages
docs.text:
Code sets, coverage policies, and risk models change every year. The workflows, skills, and medical tools use reference data that does not update with the software, and OpenMed does not promise that hosted data will follow each new release of ICD-10-CM, CPT, HCC models, or coverage determinations.

  • Check the model, payment year, and segment shown in each coding report.
  • The hosted service loads one ICD-10 fiscal year at a time. A code retired in that year shows as not in the reference set, even for an earlier encounter, and a code added after the HCC tables were published shows no HCC category. For retrospective work, check the code against the release that applied on the encounter date.
  • Treat risk scores as estimates. They are not CMS payment determinations.
  • Verify codes, coverage, and scores against the current official source before billing, submission, or any clinical use.

A reviewer remains responsible for every output, as with any version of OpenMed.

docs.title: Keep your installation safe
docs.text:
• Keep a copy of the installed binary. Your install link depends on OpenMed-hosted services. A saved copy does not. On macOS, copy the versioned folder under ~/.local/share/openmed/; on Linux, copy ~/.local/bin/openmed. Keep the copy somewhere else, because openmed update removes older versions from the install folder.
  • Back up what matters. Your settings, sessions, and custom skills are in ~/.openmed/. That folder also contains your credentials, so protect any backup accordingly.

  • Watch the session folder. Sessions keep large tool results on disk. To see how much space they use:

    du -sh ~/.openmed/sessions

    Folders in ~/.openmed/sessions/ belong to individual sessions. Deleting one removes that session and its saved results, and it cannot be resumed afterwards.

docs.title: Operating systems
docs.text: OpenMed 1.0 was built for macOS on Apple Silicon and for Linux on x86-64 (GNU libc). Future operating system releases may stop running it, and no rebuilt binary will follow the final 1.0.x update. If you depend on OpenMed, test operating system upgrades before you roll them out.

docs.title: Getting help
docs.text: The documentation on this site is the reference for 1.0. There is no obligation to provide support, but you can still reach OpenMed through the support page.

docs.title: MCP Connectors
docs.text:
OpenMed can discover remote MCP servers and expose their tools inside the same agent loop as the native tool registry. MCP is optional, user-configured, and separate from the built-in native tools.

No MCP servers are configured by default.

docs.title: Native vs MCP
docs.text:
These capabilities already ship natively and do not require MCP:

  • extraction and PII tooling such as extract_entities, extract_pii, and deidentify_text
  • terminology and literature tools such as search_pubmed, search_icd10_codes, lookup_cpt_code, lookup_snomed_code, and HCC helpers
  • deterministic workflows
  • built-in skills

Use MCP for external systems that are not already part of the native OpenMed surface, such as internal policy services, registries, payer tools, institutional knowledge hubs, or other organization-specific systems.

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
Default path:

~/.config/openmed/mcp_servers.json

Override it with:

export OPENMED_MCP_CONFIG_PATH=/path/to/mcp_servers.json

OpenMed bootstraps the file automatically on first MCP-aware CLI or TUI use.

Schema:

{
  "version": 1,
  "servers": [
    {
      "id": "guidelines_hub",
      "name": "Guidelines Hub",
      "url": "https://example.com/mcp",
      "enabled": true,
      "timeout_seconds": 20,
      "extra_headers": {}
    }
  ]
}

Validation rules:

  • url must be HTTPS
  • id must start with a letter, use lowercase letters, digits, or underscores, and be at most 63 characters
  • timeout_seconds must be between 1 and 120

Values in extra_headers are stored in this file as plain text. To keep a token out of the file, use the header override under Environment overrides.

docs.title: CLI management
docs.text:
openmed mcp list
openmed mcp add guidelines_hub https://example.com/mcp --name "Guidelines Hub"
openmed mcp enable guidelines_hub
openmed mcp disable guidelines_hub
openmed mcp enable --all
openmed mcp disable --all
openmed mcp set-url guidelines_hub https://new-url.example.com/mcp
openmed mcp remove guidelines_hub
openmed mcp doctor
openmed mcp doctor --all
openmed mcp doctor guidelines_hub

add enables the new server. doctor checks enabled servers unless you name one or pass --all. It is the quickest way to confirm that a URL is actually a live JSON-RPC MCP endpoint rather than a marketing page or docs site.

The global --mcp-enabled flag enables every configured server before the command runs, and that change stays in the config file.

docs.title: Environment overrides
docs.text:
For a server ID such as guidelines_hub, OpenMed checks:

  • OPENMED_MCP_GUIDELINES_HUB_ENABLED
  • OPENMED_MCP_GUIDELINES_HUB_URL
  • OPENMED_MCP_GUIDELINES_HUB_HEADERS_JSON

Example:

export OPENMED_MCP_GUIDELINES_HUB_ENABLED=true
export OPENMED_MCP_GUIDELINES_HUB_URL=https://example.com/mcp
export OPENMED_MCP_GUIDELINES_HUB_HEADERS_JSON='{"Authorization":"Bearer ..."}'

docs.title: How MCP tools appear
docs.text:
Discovered remote tools are namespaced as:

mcp__<server_id>__<tool_name>

They are added to the agent's tool list during discovery. Characters a tool name cannot use are replaced, and a name longer than 64 characters is shortened.

docs.title: Discovery and caching
docs.text:
OpenMed discovers tools from enabled servers at runtime and caches the result.

Cache behavior:

  • cache file: ~/.config/openmed/mcp_tools_cache.json
  • override path: OPENMED_MCP_TOOLS_CACHE_PATH
  • override TTL: OPENMED_MCP_TOOLS_CACHE_TTL_SECONDS (default 3600)

The cache exists to reduce repeated startup/discovery overhead when MCP is enabled.

docs.title: TUI usage
docs.text:
In the TUI:

  • type # to browse enabled MCP namespaces
  • run /mcp to inspect configured servers, URLs, enabled state, and discovered-tool counts

If openmed mcp doctor reports that a server returned HTML, the configured URL is not the live MCP JSON-RPC endpoint.

docs.title: Boundary notes
docs.text:
MCP is an extension surface, not a replacement for the native tool inventory.

Important trust boundary notes:

  • remote MCP servers are user-configured and open-ended, so they are not counted among the built-in native tools
  • OpenMed treats discovered MCP tools as PHI-gated, so deid and strict modes refuse them. In full mode, the agent can send clinical text to them. This is not a substitute for your own deployment, policy, or compliance controls
  • once you add a remote MCP server, its network, auth, retention, and privacy behavior become part of your real system boundary

You can add MCP servers and local skills. There is no CLI for registering new native medical backends.

docs.title: Native Medical Services
docs.text:
OpenMed operates across three boundaries:

  • the local operator runtime
  • the configured model-provider path for general agent reasoning
  • the native medical services that power extraction, de-identification, terminology, and HCC/RAF work

The split lets long clinical text and coding work go to dedicated services instead of through the chat model on every pass. It does not make that work local. Text sent to a native medical service leaves your machine, and that service receives it.

By default, OpenMed binaries use the OpenMed-hosted medical services. You can point either service plane at your own compatible server; see Use your own service endpoints.

Reference architecture Local runtime. Separate medical services. Explicit boundary.

OpenMed keeps sessions, plans, workflow previews, and artifacts in the operator runtime while general agent reasoning uses the configured model provider. Clinical extraction and medical-coding services sit behind a separate native service plane, so page-heavy work does not all have to go through the chat model. Text sent to these services leaves your machine.

Plane 01 Operator runtime

CLI, TUI, sessions, plans, provenance, and workflow artifacts remain on the operator machine, with the review loop visible before teams depend on outputs.

Local runtime Review surface Artifact control Plane 02 Clinical extraction service

NER, PII detection, de-identification, and batch extraction run through the native service plane.

Native extraction PII detection De-identification Plane 03 Medical coding and terminology service

ICD-10, CPT, SNOMED, LOINC, HCC mapping, and RAF scoring run through a separate service boundary. PubMed, MedlinePlus, and RxNorm lookups go from your machine to those public APIs by default.

Terminology service LOINC / RxNorm / MedlinePlus HCC / RAF Default deployment Hosted by default, configurable by you.

OpenMed operates the medical-service tier as hosted native infrastructure, so no self-hosting is needed to get started. Each service plane can be pointed at a compatible server you operate with a configuration change, without changing the workflow surface.

OpenMed-hosted services Native runtime integration Your own endpoints

docs.title: Clinical extraction plane
docs.text:
For practical prompts, language and redaction controls, document previews, batch processing and extraction exports, see the Clinical NLP guide.

The extraction plane is the native service boundary for clinical text processing.

It powers native OpenMed tools such as:

  • extract_entities
  • extract_pii
  • deidentify_text
  • deidentify_batch
  • batch extraction workflows built on the same service

Operationally, this is where OpenMed handles:

  • clinical NER
  • billing-oriented entity extraction
  • PII detection
  • de-identification

Configuration:

  • binaries use the OpenMed-hosted extraction service by default
  • OPENMED_INFERENCE_URL points this plane at your own compatible server
  • the service boundary can move without changing the local workflow surface

The extraction service receives the text or document bytes sent to it.

docs.title: Coding and terminology plane
docs.text:
The coding plane is the native service boundary for terminology, education, and risk adjustment.

It powers native OpenMed tools such as:

  • PubMed search and abstract retrieval
  • ICD-10, CPT, SNOMED, and LOINC search / lookup / validation
  • RxNorm medication normalization and related-concept lookup
  • MedlinePlus patient-education topic lookup
  • code crosswalks
  • CCSR categories, Charlson and Elixhauser comorbidity indices, and Orphanet rare-disease lookups
  • HCC, RxHCC, and ESRD mapping
  • RAF, RxHCC, and ESRD score calculation

OpenMed can review a clinical note, extract coding candidates, and then pass those codes to the terminology and HCC service for checking.

Configuration:

  • binaries use the OpenMed-hosted coding and terminology service by default
  • OPENMED_MED_CODES_API_URL points this plane at your own compatible server
  • PubMed, MedlinePlus, and RxNorm lookups run directly from your machine to those public APIs by default
  • the service boundary can move without changing the local workflow surface

The coding service receives the codes, search text, and values such as age and sex sent to it.

docs.title: Interpreting code validation and HCC results
docs.text:
For ICD-10 validation, valid describes the code's format. Check exists and billable separately before accepting a coding candidate. A category such as N18.3 can have an accepted format while being absent from the loaded billable code set. Conversely, three-character codes such as I10 can be billable; code length and the lookup's standalone sequencing flag are not billability checks. Use the reference release appropriate to the encounter date.

For CPT validation, valid: null means the result is unconfirmed: the code service does not list the code and the LCD cross-check was unavailable. It does not mean the code is invalid. Try again in a few minutes.

For retrospective HCC work, pass the exact payment_year and model_segment, and retain the service's reference provenance. If the service does not support the requested year, OpenMed retries with a supported year and adds a warning, so check the year the result used. A model's agreement with a tool result does not verify the mapping table or RAF score. Treat missing reference data and service errors as missing evidence requiring review.

RAF, RxHCC, and ESRD scores are estimates. Full parity with the official CMS risk-adjustment software has not been validated, so every score result and workflow artifact says so, names the model, payment year, and segment used, and lists submitted codes that received no HCC category. Verify scores before billing or submission.

Coding workflows score at most 50 submitted codes for HCC mapping and RAF. The report marks the run DEGRADED and lists any further codes as not scored, so the RAF does not include them.

docs.title: When a service is unavailable
docs.text:
Hosted services can restart or have short outages, and they are provided as available: they may change, be interrupted, or be discontinued. See Long-Term Use for what depends on them. OpenMed reports an outage instead of guessing:

  • Tools return an error saying the service is unavailable, instead of an empty result.
  • Workflows that need reference data, such as prior authorization (LCD criteria) and appeal review (denial codes), stop with an error instead of producing a review against empty data.
  • Coding workflows mark the artifact DEGRADED and name each service step that failed. RAF is reported as "not calculated" rather than estimated locally.
  • Skill instructions report that they are temporarily unavailable, and come back without a restart once the service is reachable.

Re-run the request once the service is reachable again.

docs.title: Why the split matters
docs.text:
The split has practical effects:

  • extraction and de-identification can scale independently from coding and terminology lookup
  • page-heavy clinical inputs do not need to consume chat-model context for every extraction or coding pass
  • the model-provider path stays separate from the extraction and coding services
  • either service can be replaced without changing the operator workflow surface

The split does not keep data away from the chat model by itself. Text in the conversation and many tool results reach the model, including sample entities from extract_entities. The dedicated privacy tools return summaries instead; see Clinical file review.

These service planes are native OpenMed backends. They are not remote MCP servers.

docs.title: Deployment patterns
docs.text:
Pattern Runtime Extraction / PII Coding / HCC Default (hosted) Local operator machine OpenMed-hosted native extraction endpoint OpenMed-hosted native coding and terminology endpoint Your own endpoints Local operator machine Compatible server you operate Compatible server you operate

You can mix the two: each plane is configured separately.

docs.title: Security and access model
docs.text:
OpenMed does not claim that any deployment is compliant. What it does state is narrower:

  • sessions, plans, tool calls, and review steps are visible to the operator
  • the model-provider path and the medical-service tier are separate, explicit boundaries
  • the actual privacy and compliance posture depends on where those services are hosted and governed
  • no product telemetry is built into the runtime

By default, OpenMed serves the native medical-service tier so you do not need to deploy it yourself. The same workflow surface can target a compatible server you operate.

docs.title: Use your own service endpoints
docs.text:
Standard binaries use OpenMed's native services without extra local setup. To run either service plane on your own infrastructure, point OpenMed at a compatible server you operate. Each plane is configured separately, so you can move one and keep the other hosted.

A custom service URL receives only the API key or token you configure for that service.

Built-in skills and workflow reference data still come from OpenMed-hosted services, even when both planes use your own servers.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text:
Variable Purpose OPENMED_INFERENCE_URL Base URL of the extraction / PII / de-id service OPENMED_INFERENCE_API_KEY Sent as X-API-Key to the extraction service OPENMED_INFERENCE_HF_TOKEN Hugging Face token for a private Space, sent as X-HF-Authorization OPENMED_INFERENCE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS Request timeout for the extraction service OPENMED_MED_CODES_API_URL Base URL of the coding and terminology service OPENMED_MED_CODES_API_KEY Sent as X-API-Key to the coding service OPENMED_MED_CODES_HF_TOKEN Hugging Face token for a private Space, sent as Authorization: Bearer OPENMED_MED_CODES_TIMEOUT_SECONDS Request timeout for the coding service OPENMED_MED_CODES_EXECUTION_MODE client (default) runs PubMed, MedlinePlus, and RxNorm from your machine; server sends them through the coding service OPENMED_NCBI_API_KEY Your own NCBI E-utilities key for higher PubMed rate limits OPENMED_SHARED_API_KEY / OPENMED_SHARED_HF_TOKEN One key or token for both services OPENMED_SERVICE_SECRETS_PATH Read the file below from a different path

Environment variables win over the file. Restart OpenMed after changing either.

docs.title: ~/.openmed/service_secrets.json
docs.text:
The same settings can live in a file, so they persist across shells:

{
  "inference": {
    "base_url": "https://nlp.internal.example.org",
    "api_key": "{env:OPENMED_NLP_KEY}"
  },
  "med_codes": {
    "base_url": "https://codes.internal.example.org",
    "api_key": "{env:OPENMED_CODES_KEY}",
    "ncbi_api_key": "{env:NCBI_API_KEY}"
  }
}
  • Every field is optional. A plane without base_url keeps using the hosted default.
  • hf_token is accepted in either section for a private Hugging Face Space.
  • A shared section with api_key or hf_token applies to both services.
  • "{env:NAME}" reads the value from the environment variable NAME, so the file does not need to contain the secret itself.
  • ncbi_api_key is your own NCBI E-utilities key for higher PubMed rate limits.
  • Keep the file private: chmod 600 ~/.openmed/service_secrets.json.

To check which endpoints are in use, run openmed env; it shows whether each service uses the OpenMed-hosted default or your custom URL, and never prints keys.

See Privacy & Security for the runtime-boundary explanation.

docs.title: Privacy & Security
docs.text: OpenMed is built for environments where operators need to see what the system is doing, where data is stored, and which external services are in the loop. This page describes what the product does.

docs.title: Runtime boundary
docs.text:
OpenMed itself runs locally. The TUI, session files, plans, cards, workflow artifacts, and local file operations all happen on your machine.

That does not mean every clinical capability is fully offline. Many medical functions depend on remote service boundaries:

  • The model or batch provider (openmed login / OPENAI_API_KEY / ANTHROPIC_API_KEY / OPENROUTER_API_KEY / MIMO_API_KEY / DOUBLEWORD_API_KEY, or a configured custom endpoint)
  • OpenMed's native medical service plane for extraction, PII, de-identification, terminology, HCC, and RAF tooling. By default these are OpenMed-hosted services, and they receive the text sent to them
  • Public reference APIs for PubMed, MedlinePlus, and RxNorm lookups, which receive the search terms sent to them
  • User-added remote MCP endpoints

If you configure OpenRouter, prompts for general agent reasoning go to OpenRouter and on to whichever upstream provider serves the model you selected — one more hop than a direct OpenAI or Anthropic key. Review OpenRouter's privacy settings for how they handle and log your data. Provider credentials are never mixed: an OpenRouter key is only ever sent to OpenRouter, and an OpenAI or Anthropic key is never sent there.

With the MiMo provider, model requests go directly to https://token-plan-ams.xiaomimimo.com/v1 using your tp token-plan key. This is hosted inference; a token-plan subscription does not make the model local or offline. Workflow helper requests use the same provider and selected model. MiMo does not borrow another provider's credentials.

Doubleword real-time, Responses and Batch requests send their input to https://api.doubleword.ai/v1 and to the infrastructure serving the selected model. OpenMed stores the staged input and downloaded output/error JSONL under ~/.openmed/batches/ with owner-only permissions. It never stores the key in that job record. Individual Responses request/output snapshots are stored under ~/.openmed/responses/ with owner-only permissions. Direct JSON/JSONL input is not automatically de-identified, and TUI PHI mode does not transform it. Responses background jobs retain remote state for retrieval. See Doubleword before submitting sensitive data.

OpenMed does not assume every task belongs on the same remote boundary. General agent reasoning uses the configured model provider, while extraction, PII, de-identification, terminology, HCC, and RAF paths use dedicated medical services. This split keeps long or repetitive clinical processing out of the chat model. It does not make that processing local. The actual privacy and compliance posture depends on where those services are hosted and governed.

docs.title: Approval And Review Model
docs.text:
OpenMed does not stop for a modal approval before every tool call.

  • Deterministic workflows use a separate draft/finalize lifecycle, where final writes require an explicit host action plus a verified immutable draft snapshot
  • Final workflow bundles are staged privately and committed atomically only to a new, empty, or matching OpenMed-owned output directory; protected state and arbitrary nonempty directories fail closed
  • In the default ask access mode, tools that write or edit files, such as write_file, edit_file, and save_jsonl, show an approval dialog. Use /access to change the mode: read-only allows only read-only tools, and full-access runs tools without per-call approval
  • --auto-approve and /autoapprove skip those dialogs and log each bypassed prompt. They do not cover workflow final writes or clinical review drafts, and they do not release PHI mode or file privacy restrictions
  • Read/search/extraction tools can run without a modal approval step, but their execution is still surfaced in the TUI with plans, tool-call messages, and results. This includes tools that send text to a native medical service, and fetch_web_page
  • Headless openmed agent --once cannot show a dialog. Approval-gated tools are denied unless you pass --auto-approve, and workflow finalization and clinical review drafts are refused

For stricter rules, use deny_tools and ask_tools in runtime settings.

docs.title: Clinical file review
docs.text:
Start with the Clinical NLP guide for examples, redaction methods, language controls, PDF/image drafts and resumable batches.

For dedicated redaction, give deidentify_text the source file_path and requested output_path directly. The tool reads supported content internally, sends it to the configured NLP service, and returns counts, status and the output path. Reading the raw file into the conversation first can disclose it to the chat model.

File privacy is off by default. Select its mode with a host command:

Command Effect /privacy-chat off Disable file privacy restrictions. Prompts do not turn them on. /privacy-chat on Activate restrictions immediately. /privacy-chat is a shorthand. /privacy-chat auto Clear any active restriction and wait for a recognized file privacy request.

You can change modes in the same session after the current turn finishes or stops. The command alone changes the setting without sending a model request. To also send a request, append it: /privacy-chat on Deidentify /path/note.txt. The shorter /privacy-chat Deidentify /path/note.txt form does the same. Attachments and file aliases are retained.

Only opt-in auto mode uses local phrase recognition. Familiar explicit prompts such as “Deidentify /path/note.txt” and “Mask personal info” with an attached file activate the restriction. Actions such as "extract" must directly refer to personal identifiers. Extracting clinical entities and mentioning patient identifiers elsewhere in a report request does not activate it. Recognition does not cover every language or wording; select on when it misses a request. Once triggered, auto stays active across follow-ups until you select off or reselect auto.

Once active, the host allows only inspect_file, deidentify_text, extract_pii, deidentify_batch and update_plan from its trusted built-in implementations. General readers, code execution, external tools and provider built-ins are blocked, including guessed tool calls and generic auto-approval. Attachments reach the chat model as paths only. The setting persists across follow-ups, model changes, session resume and forks, including whether auto has already activated. off restores the tools allowed by the other session controls; it does not change PHI or access mode. A fresh conversation with /clear starts with file privacy off. Ordinary model requests and history resets cannot release an active restriction.

For headless runs, pass --file-privacy off, on or auto with openmed agent --once. The default is off.

This restriction covers subsequent tool dispatch and attachment payloads. It does not scrub raw text pasted into a prompt, earlier conversation content or existing system instructions, and cannot undo earlier reads or tool side effects. A tool already running when the restriction activates has its later result, exception and progress withheld. Global FULL, DEID and STRICT modes remain separate controls. The dedicated privacy tools still send source content to the configured NLP service.

The clinical profile accepts automatic or explicit language (de, DE, de-DE), patient/clinician roles, redaction categories and clinical preservation. It supports mask, remove, localized replacement, managed keyed hashing and explicit date shifting. The full date of birth is redacted. A higher detection threshold can leave more identifiers visible; it is not a general safety setting.

The service gates output by language, model qualification and policy controls. When a request needs a review draft, deidentify_text refuses with “This request requires explicit review” and writes nothing. A review draft needs your explicit opt-in:

  • In /privacy and /privacy-batch, select Allow an unqualified draft for my review.
  • In chat, the agent sends review_mode=true and OpenMed shows a dialog for that exact request. A model-supplied review_mode=true is not consent, and auto-approval does not answer the dialog.
  • Headless openmed agent --once cannot grant this consent, so the request fails with no output.

Review drafts return needs_review. They are drafts for inspection, not clinically validated anonymization. Partial coverage and failed processing do not write an output. Writes are atomic and owner-only; source collisions and existing outputs are rejected unless a separate output is explicitly authorized for replacement.

In the TUI, /privacy opens a local review screen with language, method, role and category controls. It requires FULL mode and never changes PHI mode itself. Preview text stays outside the chat transcript and audit payload, although the source still goes to the configured NLP service. “Save shown output” writes that exact preview, rejects a changed source and makes no second service call.
